messages.author: e1c430550f86b1f6
messages.subject: multiple missing data(x) in MVN/GP
parts:
Hi all,

I am wondering if anyone has some expereince in handling multple missing data (x) with STAN in a MV/GP context.

For a very simple model is as follow

x ~ MVN (0, Sigma)

Let's assume I have the following x:

[  0.01, NA,   NA,
  -0.02, NA,   NA,
   0.05, NA,   0.02,
     NA, 0.03, -0.01 ]

Note that for row 1 and row 2, we have 2 missing values per "observation"

[ 0.01, NA, NA]
[-0.02, NA, NA]


If i just follow the manual and declare them as paramters (vector[6] x_miss) and create a new matrix as:

x_new <-
[ 0.01, x_miss[1], x_miss[2],
 -0.02, x_miss[3], x_miss[4],
  0.05, x_miss[5], 0.02,
x_miss[6], 0.03, -0.01]

x_new ~ multi_normal(0, Sigma)

Q1: Following the menu, x_miss is not given any prior. If the columns are indeed somehow correlated, would this create any issue?

Q2: If i have some prior information about the mean and variance (but not the correlation) on the missing data, is it possible to encode this?

Q3: Extending this to a GP with MV input (x) that has multiple missing values, can I handle the declaration if I have no prior information on the missing value (Q1) and some prior information (Q2).

Many thanks,

Andy

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] multiple missing data(x) in MVN/GP
parts:
You’d have to break the full covariance down into marginals
and fit each pattern of missing information with the appropriate
marginal multivariate normal. Because everything is Gaussian
it can be done analytically but it would be tedious.
